title: Magnet.fla Scene 5 Symbol 6 MovieClip frozen on frame 1 (doesn't play internal frames)
description:
## Symptom (user report)
Importing Magnet.fla (fixtures/) and playing the published SWF: in Scene 5, the
"Symbol 6" MovieClip on "Layer 5" (a masked layer) does NOT play its internal
frames — it is frozen on frame 1. The MC has 16 keyframes spanning 74 frames
across 3 layers with 20 tweens. The user added trace("frame 1")/trace("frame 2")
inside the MC and only "frame 1" ever logged.

## Repro (CONFIRMED at runtime in headless Ruffle 0.2.0)
The import + symbolType classification + loop-control synthesis are all CORRECT.
The freeze is at the runtime-playback layer: a structurally-complete nested
DefineSprite never advances its own playhead.

- Symbol 6 = library item `symbol-81-*`, name "Symbol 6", correctly classified
  symbolType="movieclip" (3 layers, keyframe indices 0..73 => 74-frame span, 20
  tweens). (There is a second smaller "Symbol 6" = `symbol-42-*`, 1 layer, 1
  frame — NOT the user's MC.)
- Scene 5 (doc.scenes[1]) layer "Layer 5" (masked) frame 0 places symbol-81 once
  (single keyframe, persists), imported with loopMode="single-frame" (the binary
  per-instance loop-mode byte, exactly as task 1124 describes for movieclips).

Direct runtime proof (standalone SWF placing only Symbol 6 on a multi-frame root,
loaded into bundled Ruffle, root-level frame script `trace('cf=' + mc._currentframe)`):
  cf=1, cf=1, cf=1, ... (forever) — max _currentframe observed = 1.
The MC is VISIBLE (renders its frame-1 content) but its playhead never advances.
A second control SWF whose ROOT keyframes alternate two symbols animates fine
(screenshot diff 148270) — so the root timeline ticks/plays correctly; only the
nested MovieClip's own timeline is frozen. A second nested MC (Symbol 27,
symbol-65, 19-frame span) is ALSO frozen the same way — this is general to nested
MCs, not specific to Symbol 6.

## Root cause — NOT (a)/(b)/(c)/(d) from the loop-control family
All four hypothesized causes are RULED OUT by swf-dump of the published SWF:
- (a) symbolType: Symbol 6 imports correctly as "movieclip"
  (packages/core/src/fla/flash8-import.ts:1641-1644 SYMBOL_TYPES; :2073-2074).
  NOT misclassified as "graphic". So the graphic-only loop synthesis does not apply.
- (b) loop-control synthesis: the gate is INTACT and reached. In the published
  SWF the Symbol 6 PlaceObject2 carries NO clipActions (no synthesized
  gotoAndStop(1)). Verified: the FIRST-PLACEMENT gate
  packages/swf/src/compiler/frames.ts:885-888 computes isGraphicInstance=false ->
  loopMode="loop" for symbol-81 (instrumented log:
  `[DBG FIRST-PLACE] sym=symbol-81-... type=movieclip rawLoopMode=single-frame -> loopMode=loop isGraphic=false`).
  The MOVE path is never hit for this single placement. All 1466 @flash/swf unit
  tests pass (loopmode.test.ts "movieclip instances ignore loopMode" green).
  NOTE for follow-up: the MOVE path packages/swf/src/compiler/frames.ts:1435
  (`const moveLoopMode = displayObj.loopMode ?? "loop"`) is NOT gated on
  symbolType==="graphic" the way the first-placement path (886) and sprite.ts
  (234) are — a latent gap that would mis-synthesize on a moved movieclip with
  loopMode="single-frame", but it does NOT cause THIS freeze (Symbol 6 is a single
  persistent placement).
- (c) DefineSprite frame emission: COMPLETE. The Symbol 6 sprite (spriteId from
  charIdMap; swf-dump id 218 in full Magnet / id 234 standalone) emits all 74
  ShowFrames with PlaceObject2 moves on every frame (motion tweens) and
  RemoveObject/re-place at keyframes. Authored stop() frame scripts appear at
  sprite-frames 24/44/73 only (bytecode 07960100031700 = Stop; ...). The maxFrames
  is correctly computed via layerFrameCount() (74), not l.frames.length (16).
- (d) No stop() on the MC's frame 1. First stop is at sprite-frame 24.

So the published SWF is structurally a correct, auto-playing nested DefineSprite,
yet Ruffle holds it on frame 1. The defect is therefore in the runtime-playback
contract of the emitted SWF for nested sprites (something Ruffle reads to decide
the child sprite is stopped), NOT in the import classification or the loop-control
clip-action synthesis.

## Where to look next (fix direction)
1. There appears to be NO existing e2e oracle that proves a NESTED MovieClip
   advances its OWN timeline in headless Ruffle (motion-tween.spec.ts only
   exercises a ROOT-timeline tween). Add one as the acceptance oracle: place a
   multi-frame MC on the root once, run in bundled Ruffle, assert mc._currentframe
   advances past 1 over ticks (the exact harness used to prove this bug: 2-frame
   root with `trace('cf=' + mc._currentframe)`, read via player.traceObserver).
2. Investigate why the child DefineSprite does not tick: compare a known-good
   third-party SWF with an animating nested MC against ours, tag-by-tag (header
   FileAttributes — ours decoded as empty {}; SetBackgroundColor; the DefineSprite
   SpriteID/FrameCount; whether the nested ShowFrame count vs declared FrameCount
   match; AVM1 root DoAction that might call stop() on children). Check whether a
   stray stop()/global SWF flag or a missing/incorrect FileAttributes/initial-play
   state causes Ruffle to leave nested sprites paused. Confirm against
   ruffle/core/src/display_object/movie_clip.rs run_frame / playing default.
3. If a CLEAN (non-Magnet) compiled multi-frame MC also freezes, the bug is in the
   compiler's sprite/root emission; if only Magnet-imported MCs freeze, look at an
   import-specific artifact on the timeline/frames.

## Priority
HIGH — an entire MovieClip's animation does not play (core playback). Likely
affects every nested MovieClip in every imported FLA, not just Symbol 6.

## Evidence artifacts (reproducible)
- Standalone build: load Magnet.fla, place only symbol-81 on a multi-frame root,
  compileDocument({compress:false}); swf-dump shows the 74-frame sprite + a clean
  PlaceObject2 (no clipActions).
- Runtime: bundled Ruffle traceObserver yields cf=1 forever for mc._currentframe.

================================================================================
## QA RE-INVESTIGATION (e2e-agent, HEAD 84378a0) — PREMISE IS WRONG; NOT A DEFECT
================================================================================

**Verdict: NOT REPRODUCIBLE / NOT A BUG.** Symbol 6 (the user's reported MC) plays
correctly. The "second frozen MC" (Symbol 27) is frozen BY ITS OWN AUTHORED
SCRIPT, which is the .fla's design. There is no compiler or runtime-playback
defect. RECOMMEND closing as `cancelled` (works-as-designed) after the worker
confirms the user's real symptom (below).

### What was actually verified at runtime (bundled Ruffle 0.2.0, traceObserver)
Built minimal + Magnet-derived repros, compiled via `compileDocument({compress:false})`,
loaded in real Ruffle, read `mcInst._currentframe` per tick via a root frame script
+ `player.traceObserver`. ALSO confirmed visually (red square tracked at two distinct
x-ranges 50..202 and 199..289 across frames — it genuinely animates):

1. **Symbol 6 = symbol-81 (the USER's MovieClip): PLAYS.** `_currentframe` advances
   1..25 then holds at 25. Its OWN frame scripts are `stop()` ONLY at frame 24/44/73 —
   NO stop() on frame 1. It animates frames 1->24 then stops (authored). Confirmed in:
   minimal clean doc, masked-layer placement (mimicking Scene 5 "Layer 5" mask), and
   under a stopped root (`stop()` on root frame 1, like Scene 2/Scene 5). ALL advance.
2. **A minimal clean 2-keyframe movieclip (square x=0 -> x=200): PLAYS** (cf alternates
   1<->2; visually moves).
3. **Symbol 27 = symbol-65 (the task's claimed "general nested-MC freeze"): FROZEN —
   BUT BY DESIGN.** Its OWN timeline frame 0 (layer 0) carries the AUTHORED frame script
   `stop()`. The emitted DefineSprite (id 158) frame 1 begins with the exact bytecode
   `07 96 01 00 03 17 00` = `Stop; Push undefined; Pop; End` — i.e. the authored
   `stop()`. The MC is DESIGNED to sit on frame 1 until external game logic calls
   `play()` (its frame-9 script does `_parent.play()` / `play()` when `tgt` is set;
   frame-10 `play()`). Placing it ALONE with no game logic leaves it correctly stopped.

### Why the prior investigation reached the wrong conclusion
The prior standalone repro placed symbol-65 (or symbol-81 in a context that never
ticked the child) with NO authored game logic to ever call play(), so a sprite that
SHOULD stop on its own frame 1 (symbol-65) read cf=1 forever — and that was
mis-generalized to "nested MovieClips don't advance". The structural swf-dump checks
in the original ticket (sprite has all frames, no synthesized gotoAndStop(1), maxFrames
correct) were all TRUE and CORRECT — the sprite WAS complete; the `stop()` at sprite
frame 1 is an AUTHORED DoAction the dump-summary did not decode. There is no missing
FileAttributes / play-state / runtime-contract defect: a sprite with no frame-1 stop
auto-plays in Ruffle exactly as expected.

### Compiler/runtime are correct — NO file:line fix
- DefineSprite numFrames + per-frame ShowFrames + PlaceObject moves are all emitted
  correctly (`packages/swf/src/sprite.ts` encodeDefineSprite; maxFrames via
  layerFrameCount()). symbol-81 sprite id 234 = 74 ShowFrames; symbol-65 sprite id 158
  = 19 ShowFrames. No FrameCount=1 collapse.
- The authored `stop()` on symbol-65 frame 0 is correctly compiled to a frame-1
  DoAction (Stop opcode 0x07). That is the .fla's content, not a defect.
- The latent MOVE-path loopMode gate gap noted originally
  (`packages/swf/src/compiler/frames.ts:~1435` `moveLoopMode = displayObj.loopMode ??
  "loop"` not gated on symbolType==="graphic") is REAL but does NOT cause this — and
  did NOT trigger for either symbol (single persistent placements). Leave as the
  separate latent follow-up it already is.

### REMAINING QUESTION for the worker (the user's REAL symptom)
The user said Symbol 6 was "frozen on frame 1" and only `trace("frame 1")` logged.
But at HEAD symbol-81 PLAYS. Two possibilities the worker should pin against the
user's actual session before closing:
 (a) The user navigated the menu to a state where Symbol 6 never gets its play()
     trigger (it IS designed to advance only once, then stop at frame 24 — if the
     user only saw it on the menu/preloader it may legitimately not be ticking yet);
 (b) The user added their trace to a DIFFERENT "Symbol 6" — note there are TWO library
     items named "Symbol 6": symbol-81 (3 layers, 74-frame, the animated one) and
     symbol-42 (1 layer, 1 frame). A trace on symbol-42 would only ever log once.
Reproduce the user's exact navigation path in the published full Magnet SWF (Scene 2
menu -> Scene 5) before treating any freeze as a compiler defect.

### COVERAGE GAP CLOSED (the genuinely useful deliverable)
There was NO e2e oracle proving a nested MovieClip advances its own timeline in Ruffle
(motion-tween.spec.ts tests only the ROOT timeline). Added:
`apps/desktop/e2e/nested-movieclip-playback.spec.ts` — builds a 2-keyframe movieclip
(square x=0 -> x=200, NO frame-1 stop) on a 2-frame root, publishes via the
`__flashTest` bridge, loads in bundled Ruffle, and asserts `mcInst._currentframe`
advances past 1 via `player.traceObserver`. PASSES at HEAD. This guards against a
FUTURE regression that truly freezes a nested sprite (e.g. a stray synthesized
gotoAndStop(1) on a movieclip placement, or a sprite emitted with FrameCount 1).


================================================================================
## RESOLVED (e2e-agent, HEAD 8f3aafc) — REAL BUG, CONTEXT-SPECIFIC. FIX LANDED.
================================================================================

**The prior "NOT A BUG" verdict was an ISOLATION-TEST ARTIFACT.** It only ever
placed Symbol 6 on a SINGLE root keyframe (persisting but NOT moving), which hits
the FIRST-PLACEMENT emit path — and that path IS graphic-gated (frames.ts ~885),
so no synthesis fired and the MC played. The USER's actual Scene 5 has Symbol 6
on a layer that spans ≥2 frames AND the instance PERSISTS + MOVES across them,
which routes through the MOVE path — and the MOVE path was NOT graphic-gated.
The user CONFIRMED the visible freeze; this is a real, context-specific defect.

### Root cause (one line)
The clip-action MOVE/persist path `packages/swf/src/compiler/frames.ts:1435`
computed `moveLoopMode = displayObj.loopMode ?? "loop"` with NO
`symbolType === "graphic"` gate (unlike first-placement at ~885), so a movieclip
that persists+moves across multi-frame root frames got a synthesized
`onClipEvent(load){ this.gotoAndStop(1) }` on its MOVE PlaceObject2 — freezing the
nested clip on frame 1 from the second root frame onward.

### swf-dump evidence (2-frame root, MC moved on frame 2, loopMode="single-frame")
Before fix — frame 2 PlaceObject2 (action "modify") carried:
  clipActions: ClipActions { all_event_flags: LOAD, records: [ClipAction { events: LOAD,
    action_data: [... "this" ... "gotoAndStop" ... push 1 ...] }] }   ← this.gotoAndStop(1)
Frame 1's first-placement PlaceObject2 had NO clipActions (gated path, played fine).
After fix — the frame-2 "modify" PlaceObject2 is a clean reposition with ZERO
clipActions (swf-dump: 0 clipActions). Control: a single STATIC placement always
had 0 clipActions (which is exactly why the prior isolation test saw it "play").

### The 1124 "3 spots per file" check
- computeClipActionsKey (frames.ts:163-177): ALREADY gated (isGraphic at :172) — OK.
- first-placement emit (frames.ts:885-888): ALREADY gated (isGraphicInstance) — OK.
- MOVE emit (frames.ts:1435): WAS the missing gate. NOW FIXED. (sprite.ts:234 is
  the symbol-internal path and was already gated.)

### Fix (landed)
frames.ts move path now mirrors first-placement:
  const moveRefSymbol = symbolById.get(displayObj.symbolId);
  const moveIsGraphic = moveRefSymbol?.symbolType === "graphic";
  const moveLoopMode  = moveIsGraphic ? (displayObj.loopMode ?? "loop") : "loop";
  const moveFirstFrame= moveIsGraphic ? (displayObj.firstFrame ?? 0)    : 0;
A movieclip persisting+moving across frames no longer gets synthesized
single-frame/play-once loop-control on the move tag; a GRAPHIC still does.
Explicit user clipActions on a moved movieclip are still honoured (only the
SYNTHESIZED loop-control is suppressed).

### Regression oracles added
- Unit (loopmode.test.ts): "movieclip persisting+moving across a multi-frame root
  does NOT get synthesized loop-control on the move tag" — asserts NO HasClipActions
  (0x80) on ANY PlaceObject2. VERIFIED to FAIL on the un-fixed code, pass after.
  Plus a positive control: a GRAPHIC persisting+moving STILL gets loop-control on
  the move path (gate is symbolType-specific, not blanket suppression).
- E2E (nested-movieclip-playback.spec.ts): "a moved single-frame-loopMode movieclip
  still ticks past frame 1 (move-path graphic gate)" — publishes a 2-frame root with
  a moved MC (loopMode="single-frame"), runs in bundled Ruffle, reads
  mcInst._currentframe via traceObserver, asserts it advances past 1 (frozen MC would
  trace cf=1 forever). Both nested-MC e2e tests pass.

All 1468 @flash/swf unit tests pass (was 1466 + 2 new). Status: done (fix verified
at the SWF-byte level AND in real Ruffle).
